title: Chicken, thigh, meat and skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thighs consist of meat and skin taken from the thigh portion of a chicken. Raw thighs have a mild flavor, moderately fatty texture, and are a popular ingredient in cuisines worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken thighs contain more fat than chicken breast, making them juicier when cooked.
The skin on the thigh becomes crispy and flavorful when properly prepared.
Different cultures use thighs in traditional dishes, from French confit to Asian teriyaki.
Raw thighs are often frozen for long‑term storage without loss of quality.
Chicken thighs are a good source of iron compared with other poultry cuts.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken thighs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports the nervous system and the formation of red blood cells.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron from chicken meat helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Polyunsaturated fats
items.content: The fat in thigh skin includes beneficial polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw chicken thighs may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Processing contamination
items.content: Improper storage or cross‑contamination can cause spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thighs can be pan‑fried, baked, braised, or grilled. For crispy skin, sear on high heat then finish in the oven. Marinate in spices, soy sauce, or yogurt to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw thighs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a sealed bag; they retain quality for up to 9 months. Thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.
